question: Question linked to image nº9 A 35-year-old woman comes to the consultation because she presents chest pain when she is struggling. It does not have cardiovascular risk factors. A systolic murmur is heard in aortic focus that increases with the Valsalva maneuver. The ECG shows sinus rhythm, Q waves, repolarization disorders and left ventricular hypertrophy criteria. In the figure you can see an image of your echocardiography. Point to the FALSE option:

options.opb: This disease is associated with sudden death.
options.opc: Atrial fibrillation has a higher incidence in people with this disease.
options.opd: Dyspnea will not appear until the patient develops left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> increased risk of sudden death -> 80% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> dyspnea can occur before left ventricular systolic dysfunction -> 75% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> increased risk of atrial fibrillation -> 70% CHAIN: Aortic stenosis -> left ventricular hypertrophy -> not always a hereditary disease -> 80%
analysis: The patient is most likely presenting with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy based on the clinical presentation and echocardiography findings. This condition is commonly associated with a systolic murmur in aortic focus that increases with the Valsalva maneuver, ECG changes indicative of left ventricular hypertrophy, and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death. Atrial fibrillation can also occur in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Dyspnea may occur due to diastolic dysfunction before the development of left ventricular systolic dysfunction.
